sources.entry: Mother-of-All-Self-Hosting - Ansible playbook which helps you host services as Docker containers on your own server. AGPL-3.0 Ansible/Docker

summary.one_liner: MASH is an Ansible playbook that installs and maintains a large set of self-hosted services as Docker containers on your own server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an Ansible playbook for self-hosting services as Docker containers on your own server, with the goal of a predictable, up-to-date setup across multiple supported distros and CPU architectures. Installation, upgrades, and some maintenance tasks are automated through Ansible. The project covers a large number of services and says it will keep adding support for FOSS software. A full list of supported services is linked from the README but not included in it. Setup instructions live in the docs/ directory, and a changelog tracks backward-incompatible changes between versions. Support is offered through a Matrix room and GitHub issues.
use_cases: self-host multiple services on one server
automate installation and upgrades of self-hosted apps
run self-hosted services in Docker containers
build an all-in-one self-hosting stack with Ansible
deploy FOSS services across different Linux distros
how_to_run: Follow the README in the docs/ directory to configure and install services on your server
notable: Runs services as Docker containers for consistent setup across distros and CPU architectures
Installation, upgrades, and some maintenance are automated with Ansible
Large catalogue of supported services, with new FOSS support added over time
Changelog documents backward-incompatible changes between versions
caveats: Changes between versions are sometimes backward-incompatible, so the changelog should be checked before updating
Setup requires following the docs/ guide; the README itself gives no quick-start commands
keywords: install services on my own server
run apps in containers at home
